plan: Model the workspace as a composite tree held in one deep-copied dict: notes and references are leaves; sections and groups are containers with 'items'; the workspace itself is the root container addressed by the literal id 'workspace'.

Implement total_word_count() as a recursive fold: notes contribute regex word counts of their text with [[?id]] markers stripped first; references contribute their declared word_count; containers sum their children.
Implement unresolved_markers() as a recursive collection into a set (marker identifiers extracted from note text plus reference 'unresolved' lists), returned sorted lexicographically.
Implement outline() as a deterministic pre-order traversal emitting the workspace title, then '<kind>: <title>' per item with two spaces per nesting level (top-level items at level 1).

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check id types, locate the item and destination, reject non-container destinations, reject destinations equal to or inside the moved item's subtree (via a subtree-id set), and range-check the insertion index -- all before the single remove+insert, guaranteeing failed moves leave state untouched.
Implement to_data() as a deep copy so callers can never mutate internal state, and verify behavior with in-memory constructed fixtures using only the standard library.
mechanisms: Composite pattern: uniform recursive part-whole tree of leaves (note, reference) and containers (section, group, workspace root)
Recursive aggregation fold for word counts with kind-specific leaf contributions
Recursive set-union collection of unresolved marker identifiers with sorted deduplicated output
Deterministic pre-order depth-first traversal for indented outline rendering
Containment invariant enforcement: only containers accept children; no move of a subtree into itself or a descendant (cycle prevention via subtree-id set)
Atomic move via full up-front validation followed by a single detach/insert mutation
Defensive deep copying at construction and export to isolate internal state
